docs.title: tappack
docs.text: tappack builds a Tasmota Berry project into a .tapp package. It reads a manifest.yml, collects the project files and declared dependencies, applies channel-specific version patches, generates autoexec.be, and writes the resulting archive.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install tappack

For a one-shot run without a separate install:

uvx tappack --help

docs.title: Package a project
docs.text:
The repository includes a runnable example. From its examples directory, build it with:

cd docs/examples
tappack --module-path sample_app --output ./sample_app.tapp --channel-id development

tappack also accepts a project path from elsewhere. Run tappack --help for its options; see the quick start and manifest guide for details.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Read the tappack documentation for installation, CLI usage, manifest fields, and deployment guidance.

docs.title: Serving and remote access
docs.text:
tappack creates .tapp files; it no longer starts a web server or opens a tunnel. The former server feature was convenient during development, but it coupled an artifact builder to a long-running web process and a public-network tunnel. That added dependencies and operational behavior that packaging itself does not need, while making it easier to expose project files unintentionally.

Keep the responsibilities separate: build the archive with tappack, then publish it through a deployment or static-hosting workflow you already control. For temporary remote device access, use a separately managed tunnel tool such as tailcat rather than embedding tunnel lifecycle and exposure decisions in the packager.

The packaging command and manifest behavior are documented in the quick start and manifest reference.

docs.title: Manifest reference
docs.text:
A project can contain a manifest.yml at its root. tappack searches upward from --module-path for this file. If no manifest is found, it packages the directory using its name and does not resolve dependencies or patches.

The manifest describes the package name, version metadata, startup behavior, dependencies, and optional version patches. The runnable sample is embedded in the quick start.

docs.title: Top-level fields
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning name string Package name used in the generated autoexec.be and as the default output filename. If omitted, the project directory name is used. metadata object Optional project metadata, including the current version and Corio release settings. autoexec object Controls the generated startup file. dependencies list of objects Each object has a unique name and a dependency source. The name becomes the output subdirectory. patches list File changes applied while packaging, including channel-specific version updates.

metadata.version is the current project SemVer used as the base for automatic version patches. The Corio metadata fields org_github, org_friendly, description, docs, and link_id are optional; link_id selects a short URL to update after a Corio release. API credentials remain environment variables.

tappack generates autoexec.be from the package's Berry file paths. Set autoexec.import: true to import the package during startup; the default is false. autoexec's .channels field is a list of entries, each with a channel ID and the autoexec fields to use for that channel, as shown in the sample manifest.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Each item under dependencies has a required name and a nested source. The name selects the output subdirectory. Put .type first inside each direct source. Supported source types are:

Source Fields inside source URL .type: URL and url; the target must be a .tapp archive. Local path .type: LocalPath and path; the directory is packaged recursively. The path is resolved from the process's current working directory. GitHub release asset .type: GitHubReleaseAsset, org, repo, and filename; optionally set version and prefix. If version is omitted, the latest release is used. The default tag prefix is v.

A channel-only source contains .channels instead of a top-level .type. A direct source can also contain .channels to override itself for selected channels. The .channels list belongs inside that dependency's source, not beside the dependency entries. Each item has a channel ID and a nested dependency source. On a match, that nested source replaces the direct source; without a match, the direct source is used. A channel-only dependency with no matching entry is skipped.

The name on each dependency selects its output directory. For local sources, path is resolved from the process's current working directory. In the sample, run tappack from docs/examples: helper_package uses shared_library, while the development override for tools_package uses development_tools.

The sample manifest shows two dependency entries, one with a direct source and one with a channel override nested inside its source.

docs.title: Version patches
docs.text:
A patch entry can be a direct .type: Version patch, which applies for every channel, or a .channels list. Each channel-list item puts channel beside the .type: Version, path, and pattern fields—there is no extra patch wrapper. Only the matching channel's patch is applied; if none matches, the patch is skipped.

A version patch targets a project-relative path and a regular-expression pattern containing {version}. Without --version, Tappack increments metadata.version by inc_patch (default 1), applies the selected channel as the prerelease, and adds a build timestamp. With --version, Tappack writes that exact SemVer value into the patched file without incrementing or adding channel/build metadata. Version patches require metadata.version unless --version is supplied. The sample manifest patches src/version.be only for the development channel.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Install tappack from PyPI:

pip install tappack

The repository contains a sample project with two named dependencies. From the examples directory, package the development channel to use its local tools override and channel-specific version patch:

cd docs/examples
tappack --module-path sample_app --output ./sample_app.tapp --channel-id development

The command writes sample_app.tapp in the current directory. The manifest, Berry sources, and generated autoexec.be are stored in the archive. Dependencies are placed under their name: helper_package/ comes from the local shared_library directory, and tools_package/ uses the local development_tools directory because the development override is selected. Without that channel, tools_package/ comes from the GitHub release asset.

The example manifest is a real file used by the command above:

name: sample_app
metadata:
  version: 2.3.4

autoexec:
  import: false
  .channels:
    - channel: development
      import: true

dependencies:
  # This local package is always included under helper_package/.
  - name: helper_package
    source:
      .type: LocalPath
      path: shared_library

  # Use the released tools package by default; replace it with a local copy for development.
  - name: tools_package
    source:
      .type: GitHubReleaseAsset
      org: fmtr
      repo: tools.be
      filename: tools.tapp
      version: 0.2.1
      # This override belongs to tools_package's source; other channels use the release asset.
      .channels:
        - channel: development
          dependency:
            .type: LocalPath
            path: development_tools

patches:
  - .channels:
      - channel: development
        .type: Version
        path: src/version.be
        pattern: "var VERSION = '{version}'"

docs.title: CLI options
docs.text:
• --module-path selects the project directory. It defaults to the current directory.
  • --output selects the .tapp file. If omitted, the manifest name is used as the filename; when no manifest is present, the project directory name is used. The output is written in the current directory.
  • --channel-id selects channel-specific dependency, autoexec, and patch settings.
  • --version pins the patched Berry version exactly; it skips the automatic patch increment and channel/build suffixes.

The same scalar settings can be supplied through TAPPACK__MODULE_PATH, TAPPACK__OUTPUT, TAPPACK__CHANNEL_ID, and TAPPACK__VERSION. For example, from docs/examples:

TAPPACK__MODULE_PATH=sample_app TAPPACK__CHANNEL_ID=development tappack --output ./sample_app.tapp

Corio settings can also load a dotenv file selected with --env or a YAML file selected with --config; CLI options take precedence over environment, dotenv, and YAML values.

For an ephemeral invocation, run the same command with uvx tappack instead of tappack. Run tappack --help to see the available options.

For the manifest field reference and dependency forms, continue to the manifest guide. For the rationale behind packaging-only scope, see deployment guidance.

Replace the former server and tunnel workflow with a packaging-only CLI that builds .tapp archives from manifest.yml. Manifests support named local, URL, and GitHub-release dependencies, channel-specific dependency selection and version patches, generated autoexec.be, and exact SemVer overrides. Project metadata and releases now use Corio's release workflow.
